title: Directed pairs of generated kernel ideals
statement: Let $X$ be a quasi-compact quasi-separated scheme [def-pc-scheme, def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions]. Let $I$ be a nonempty directed preordered set, $(\mathcal S_i,\sigma_{ji})_{i\le j}$ a diagram of quasi-coherent commutative $\mathcal O_X$-algebras [def-weil-pbc-quasi-coherent-algebra], and $\mathcal J_i\subseteq\mathcal S_i$ quasi-coherent sheaves of ideals, with $\sigma_{ji}(\mathcal J_i)\subseteq\mathcal J_j$. For each $i$, let $K_i$ be a nonempty directed preordered set and $(\mathcal E_{ik},\eta_{lk})_{k\le l}$ a diagram of $\mathcal O_X$-modules [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category] of finite presentation, meaning locally cokernels of maps between finite free modules. Suppose compatible maps $\varepsilon_{ik}:\mathcal E_{ik}\to\mathcal J_i$ exhibit $\mathcal J_i$ as their colimit in modules [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit]. Put $\mathcal I_{ik}=(\varepsilon_{ik}(\mathcal E_{ik}))$, the smallest sheaf of ideals of $\mathcal S_i$ containing that image, and $\mathcal Q_{ik}=\mathcal S_i/\mathcal I_{ik}$, the sheaf quotient. Define $P=\{(i,k):i\in I,\ k\in K_i\}$ by $(i,k)\preceq(j,l)$ if $i\le j$ and $\sigma_{ji}(\mathcal I_{ik})\subseteq\mathcal I_{jl}$. Then $P$ is a small nonempty directed preorder. Its projection to $I$ is monotone, and $k\le l$ in $K_i$ implies $(i,k)\preceq(i,l)$. For every $i\le j$ and $k\in K_i$ there is $l\in K_j$ with $(i,k)\preceq(j,l)$. The quotient maps induced by $\sigma_{ji}$ make $\mathcal Q$ a diagram of quasi-coherent algebras over $P$, with $\alpha_{(j,l),(i,k)}q_{ik}=q_{jl}\sigma_{ji}$, where $q_{ik}:\mathcal S_i\to\mathcal Q_{ik}$ is the quotient map.

source.place: Properties, Tag 0817, lemma-integral-algebra-directed-colimit-finite, proof: the lifting square for E_ik to E_i′k′ using Modules 01BS; and Tag 05JS, lemma-algebra-directed-colimit-finite-presentation, proof: the ideal-containment relation on pairs.

proof.text: Each E_ik is quasi-coherent by Mathlib SheafOfModules.instIsQuasicoherentOfIsFinitePresentation. Apply (b) of [lem-weil-pbc-quasi-coherent-algebra-kernel-image-ideal] to E_ik → J_i → S_i. Choose the generated ideals and quotient algebras with their universal properties. The affine kernel formula extends to all opens: the ideal inclusion followed by q is zero on affine opens, hence zero as a module morphism; conversely ker(q) followed by the cokernel of the ideal inclusion is zero on affines, hence zero globally. Sections of kernels and the fact that a mono is the kernel of its cokernel give equality of ideals on every open.

source.place: Tag 01IC, lemma-kernel-cokernel-quasi-coherent; Section 01LA, section-quasi-coherent, items (5),(8); Properties Tags 05JS and 0817, generated-ideal quotients

proof.text: Fix i ≤ j and k. Sectionwise ideal compatibility and injectivity of J_j → S_j factor J_i → S_j through J_j, using that a monomorphism is the kernel of its cokernel in the abelian category of modules. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-finite-presentation-hom-directed-colimit] to factor E_ik → J_j through E_jl. The composite S_i → S_j → Q_jl then kills E_ik. Its module kernel represents an ideal subsheaf containing E_ik, so minimality of the generated ideal makes it contain I_ik. The kernel formula from step 1 gives the required ideal containment and extension to row j.

source.place: Tag 0817, lemma-integral-algebra-directed-colimit-finite, proof (2), lifting square; Modules Tag 01BS, lemma-finite-presentation-quasi-compact-colimit

proof.text: Reflexivity follows from $\sigma_{ii}=1$. If $(i,k)\preceq(j,l)\preceq(h,m)$, then $i\le h$ and $\sigma_{hi}(\mathcal I_{ik})=\sigma_{hj}(\sigma_{ji}(\mathcal I_{ik}))\subseteq\sigma_{hj}(\mathcal I_{jl})\subseteq\mathcal I_{hm}$, proving transitivity. The projection is monotone by definition. If $k\le l$, compatibility $\varepsilon_{ik}=\varepsilon_{il}\eta_{lk}$ gives $\mathcal I_{ik}\subseteq\mathcal I_{il}$ by minimality of generated ideals, hence row monotonicity. The set $P=\coprod_{i\in I}K_i$ is small and nonempty. For $(i,k),(j,l)$ choose $h\ge i,j$. Step 2 moves both to $(h,a),(h,b)$; choose $c\ge a,b$ in $K_h$. Row monotonicity and transitivity make $(h,c)$ a common upper bound.

source.place: Tag 05JS, lemma-algebra-directed-colimit-finite-presentation, proof, relation on pairs; Tag 0817, lifting square

proof.text: For $p=(i,k)\preceq r=(j,l)$, $q_{jl}\sigma_{ji}$ kills $\varepsilon_{ik}$ by ideal containment. The quotient universal property in [lem-weil-pbc-quasi-coherent-algebra-kernel-image-ideal](b) gives a unique algebra map $\alpha_{r,p}$ with $\alpha_{r,p}q_{ik}=q_{jl}\sigma_{ji}$. For $p\preceq r\preceq s=(h,m)$, both $\alpha_{s,r}\alpha_{r,p}$ and $\alpha_{s,p}$ have composite $q_{hm}\sigma_{hi}$ with $q_p$; uniqueness makes them equal. Likewise $\alpha_{p,p}=1$. Step 1 supplies quasi-coherence of every object, so these maps define the claimed diagram.
